units.text: Aspose.Imaging FOSS for .NET reads and writes image files across raster, vector, and specialized formats including PSD, EMF, WMF, and DICOM. It converts images between these formats and inspects their properties without requiring full decoding. The library runs on netstandard2.0 and net8.0 with no external dependencies.
Detects 14 image formats by reading only the file's signature bytes and returning an ImageFormat value, so identifying a file never requires pulling in a full imaging stack.

Reads a format's real header fields directly into an ImageInfo — width, height, bit depth, and frame count — for PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WEBP, ICO, TIFF, PSD, EMF, WMF, DICOM, DJVU, AVIF, and HEIC/HEIF, as a free open source .NET image manipulation API with no decode step.

Counts real multi-frame and multi-page content where the container format actually carries it: GIF walks its image-descriptor blocks, ICO its directory entries, TIFF its IFD chain, and a bundled multi-page DJVU (DJVM) its FORM:DJVU page components.
Provides both synchronous and async entry points for the same operation — ProbeFile()/ProbeFileAsync() and Probe()/ProbeAsync() — so a probe can run on an ASP.NET request thread without blocking it.

Never throws on a signature match it cannot fully parse — malformed or truncated input comes back as an ImageInfo with only Format set, never an exception, so a probing pipeline can run unattended over untrusted input.
Has no external dependencies, making it a lightweight alternative for .NET applications targeting netstandard2.0 or net8.0.
This example uses Aspose.Imaging FOSS for .NET to inspect an image file and report its format and frame count, helping visitors quickly verify file properties.

Aspose.Imaging FOSS for .NET exposes Aspose.Imaging FOSS for .NET as its public API surface, targeting netstandard2.0 and net8.0. The library's single entry point is ImageProbe, which provides format detection and header inspection capabilities.

Aspose.Imaging FOSS for .NET provides format detection and header inspection through ImageProbe, which includes DetectFormat, Probe, ProbeFile, ProbeAsync, and ProbeFileAsync methods, returning ImageFormat and ImageInfo values that describe the detected image format and its header-extracted properties.
The getting started guide walks through installation and a first probe step by step.
The how-to guides and FAQ provide task-focused answers for common format-detection questions.
The full API reference offers the complete browsable reference for ImageFormat, ImageInfo, and ImageProbe.
Users can open an issue on GitHub to report bugs or request features.
Aspose.Imaging FOSS for .NET reads image headers to detect formats and extract metadata via the Aspose.Imaging.Foss namespace; it targets netstandard2.0 and net8.0.

Detection and metadata only: ImageProbe identifies a format and reads its header fields; it never decodes pixel data, so there is no rendering, editing, or format-conversion capability anywhere in the library.

Frame count reflects only what the container itself records: it is a real, computed count for GIF, ICO, TIFF, and bundled multi-page DJVU (DJVM); every other supported format reports a fixed 1 for a successfully parsed header, since none of their headers carry a genuine frame or page count.

Non-placeable WMF is detected but not dimensioned: the classic (non-placeable) WMF header carries no bounding rectangle, so Probe returns a format-only ImageInfo for it; only the placeable WMF header yields Width/Height.
DICOM parsing stops at the first undefined-length element: a sequence or encapsulated pixel-data element with an undefined length ends the walk rather than being parsed.
CDR support is planned but not yet implemented: no CdrFormatHandler exists in the current source tree.

Aspose.Imaging FOSS for .NET targets netstandard2.0 and net8.0 and is built using the .NET CLI. The test project, located under tests/Aspose.Imaging.Foss.Tests, targets net9.0 and uses the xUnit test framework with test host and adapter packages, along with a code-coverage collection package. These test packages apply only to the test project and are not referenced by the main library. The repository includes a pull request workflow that validates new formats by implementing IFormatHandler and registering them in ImageProbe.
It adds full decoding, editing, rendering, and conversion across a much broader format range.
ImageFormat class lists the supported image formats including Avif, Bmp, Dicom, Emf, Gif, Heic, Ico, Jpeg, Png, Psd, and Tiff.
ImageInfo class holds read-only properties for an image's format, width, height, bit depth, and frame count, and provides a constructor to initialize them.
ImageProbe class provides methods to detect and probe image formats from files or streams, including DetectFormat, Probe, ProbeAsync, ProbeFile, and ProbeFileAsync.
